subject: Routing & token‑surge probe — A/B plan and owners (Cloudward)
messages:
From: Oliver Shaw <oliver@cloudward.ai>
To: Jordan Blake <jordan_blake@redwood.ai>
Cc: Lena Horowitz <lena.h@acme.com>
Date: 2026-11-12T14:08:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Intro + perf discovery — routing & tokens/sec

Thanks for the call earlier today, Jordan — useful conversation. Quick recap from our side:

- Cloudward runs a low‑latency conversational API for B2B customers with sustained spikes (tokens/s) during morning sync windows.
- Our current hyperscaler endpoints hold up for steady traffic but show p99 jumps during concentrated bursts; we want to understand if Redwood's routing + batch strategies can reduce p99 without sacrificing aggregate tokens/sec.

Immediate asks we have:
1) An A/B test plan that compares (a) our existing HyperscaleX endpoints vs (b) Redwood routed endpoint with model variant pinning and prefix caching enabled. Target windows: 1M tokens burst over 15 minutes, and microbursts of ~20k tokens in <30s.
2) Expected p95/p99 delta, tokens/sec sustained, and fallback behavior when capacity saturated.
3) Any constraints on model size / quantization options that affect throughput on Redwood.

I attached a short HAR with traces from today's spike and a one‑page scope doc. Oliver

From: Jordan Blake <jordan_blake@redwood.ai>
To: Oliver Shaw <oliver@cloudward.ai>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-11-13T09:17:00-08:00
Subject: Routing & token‑surge probe — internal owners and A/B plan

Oliver — thanks, that summary is exactly right and very helpful. Marissa, Ben, Karthik — looping you in to own the lab and engineering runbook. High level proposal below and a concrete set of next steps.

High level proposal (A/B):
- A: HyperscaleX (control) — Cloudward routes to existing HyperscaleX endpoints for the test windows.
- B: Redwood routed path (treatment) — route identical traffic to Redwood with: model version pinning, continuous batching enabled, KV/prefix cache warmed for common conversation prefixes, and a conservative quantized variant where applicable.
- Measure: p50/p95/p99 latency, tokens/sec sustained, tail error rate, cost per 1k tokens for each window.

Technical notes / hypotheses:
- We expect Redwood's routing + prefix caching to reduce p99 for microbursts by absorbing repeated prefixes into KV cache.
- Continuous batching should improve tokens/sec during the 15min sustained window; we need to bound added queuing latency to keep p95 within SLA.
- Quantized model variant may increase tokens/sec but could raise per‑token hallucination risk; include a small prompt test set for quality checks.

Owners and immediate asks (owners in parentheses):
- Bench runbook and infra (Ben Carter): define load patterns, generate replay traffic, set up metrics hooks (p50/p95/p99, tokens/sec, errors).
- Test harness / scripts (Karthik Iyer): provide the A/B driver, latency tracing labels, and threshold-based failover trigger.
- Eval & quality prompts (Marissa Cole): 40 prompt set for guardrail checks during the run, and golden responses for regression detection.
- Customer coordination & cutover (Jordan Blake): schedule cutover windows, share onboarding links, and coordinate HyperscaleX mirror traffic.

Attachments: I uploaded a draft test config (redwood-test-config-20261113.json) — Ben/Karthik, please iterate. Also linking HubSpot record and the Drive folder.

Next concrete steps:
1) Ben: confirm infra capacity and estimate cost delta (Redwood routing vs HyperscaleX) — due 2026-11-14 EOD.
2) Karthik: produce A/B harness and smoke script with labels — due 2026-11-15 10:00 PT.
3) Marissa: finalize prompt set and quality thresholds — due 2026-11-15 14:00 PT.
4) Jordan/Oliver: target run window 2026-11-17 08:00–08:30 PT (microburst) and 2026-11-18 09:00–09:15 PT (sustained 15min) — confirm by 2026-11-15.

I'll compile the runbook into the Drive folder when Ben/Karthik confirm capacity. Jordan

From: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>

Subject: Re: Routing & token‑surge probe — infra notes and capacity

Thanks — quick infra notes from my end after a skim of the traces Oliver sent:

- For the 15min 1M token sustained window we'll provision two dedicated Redwood pools (mixed T4x2 + A100 spare) in us-west-2 to mirror Cloudward's region. Estimate: ~120 GPU-hours for the run.
- Continuous batching parameters I'd start with: max_batch_delay_ms=15, max_batch_tokens=4096; we should record queue depth histograms to check added latency.
- For microburst runs (20k tokens <30s) we should enable an aggressive burst pool with cold‑start warmup (maintain 1 warm replica per zone) to avoid p99 spikes.
- Quantization: prefer int8 for the larger models Cloudward uses; fallback to fp16 if quality regression > 3% on Marissa's prompt set.

Action items I can take on:
- Finalize run capacity and upload infra playbook to Drive by 2026-11-14 EOD.
- Spin up a pre‑run smoke that replays the attached HAR at 50% scale to validate labels and tracing.

Ben

Subject: Confirmed: A/B plan + run windows and final asks

Oliver — thanks for the quick confirmation on the scope earlier. We have owners and an initial runbook. Quick checklist before we kick off:

- [ ] Ben to upload infra playbook and capacity estimate (due today EOD) — completed: Ben uploaded a draft to Drive.
- [ ] Karthik to share A/B harness link and smoke script (due today 10:00 PT).
- [ ] Marissa to drop the 40 prompt verification set and pass/fail criteria (due today 14:00 PT).
- [ ] Cloudward to confirm the two test windows (microburst + sustained) and provide traffic replay permission for the HAR traces.

One more ask from Cloudward we discussed that I want to call out explicitly: automated fallback policy. If p99 difference exceeds 75ms for 3 consecutive 1‑minute intervals, we should fail back to HyperscaleX for that minute while keeping logs for post‑mortem. Does that SLA‑style trigger sound right to you? If so we will implement an automated policy in the harness and surface a short incident note in the dashboard.

Oliver — if that looks good can you confirm the windows and the fallback trigger? We'll proceed to run pre‑smoke on 2026-11-16 and full runs on the agreed windows once all owners sign off.

Thanks — Jordan
